rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khaud literally means entering something; the phrase for entering water developed into an idiom for arguing and chattering in support of evil against truth.
rows.anchor: means “to enter into something.” The expression

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idiom means contentious idle talk against truth, as in Qur'anic examples at 9:69 and 42:83.
rows.anchor: idiom means to argue and chatter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowingly fabricating arguments against the truth is play with one's own intellect and that of one's followers; the Qur'an calls this attitude play.
rows.anchor: it is a form of playful attitude with one’s own intellect as well as that of one’s followers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mocking the truth is dangerous in any case, and especially so when it can lead to eternal loss.
rows.anchor: dangerous in all circumstances; however, it becomes dangerous to the ultimate degree

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressees used labels such as soothsayer, poet, fabricator, and bragger, claimed they could produce similar discourse, and said whatever came to mind to tease the Prophet; this was entertainment to them.
rows.anchor: to tease the Prophet (sws), each person would say anything that came to his mind.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb describes pushing someone forcefully and hatefully; the repeated verbal form further intensifies the force.
rows.anchor: to push someone with full force and hatred

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After their worldly pranks, they will be driven forcefully to Hell and told that this is the Fire they mocked and denied.
rows.anchor: it will be said to them that this was the Hell they would make fun of and reject in the previous world.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When warned of Hell, they called the Qur'an's warnings verbal magic to make themselves and the public indifferent to them, and are now asked whether the scene is magic or reality.
rows.anchor: they would regard these warnings of the Qur’an to be a magic of words in order to make themselves and their masses indifferent to it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As in worldly life, the deniers remain unable to see the reality before them.
rows.anchor: being able to see it.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divine command sends them into Hell, from which there is now no escape.
rows.anchor: A divine declaration will bid them to enter Hell; there is no escape for them now.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whether they endure patiently or cry out, neither response will save them or bring relief.
rows.anchor: neither will patience save them nor shouts be able to provide relief to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their punishment is the return for their own deeds; had they suffered injustice, they might expect a plea to be answered, but their exposed misdeeds leave no ground or respondent for appeal.
rows.anchor: whatever they will be facing will be because of their own misdeeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deeds are represented by their consequences, not displayed in precisely the same form they had in worldly life; this different form is still the harvest of what they sowed.
rows.anchor: it refers to their consequences.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contrasts the deniers' punishment with the reward of the righteous, meaning those who listened carefully to the Prophet's warnings, reflected, and cherished them; they will dwell in gardens and bliss.
rows.anchor: instead of making fun of the warnings of the Prophet (sws) carefully listened to them, reflected on them and held them very dear.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite, unspecified description of what their Lord grants conveys such majesty that its extent is unimaginable until recipients experience it.
rows.anchor: bears witness to enhanced majesty: no one can imagine today what their Lord will grant them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi construes “and He protected them” as coordinated with “what their Lord granted them.”
rows.anchor: In my opinion, the words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fakihin encompasses both joy and acknowledgment of divine favor, so a separate expression for gratitude is unnecessary.
rows.anchor: itself encompasses the meaning of joy and acknowledging favour; hence a separate word is not required for this meaning.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous will especially rejoice that God graciously saved them from Hell, which they see as His greatest favor; they will be wholly grateful, as expressed again in 52:26–27.
rows.anchor: the righteous will regard God’s greatest favour to be saved from the Hell these rejecters are making fun of today.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous are invited to eat and drink fully as a reward, without harm, diminishing bounty, or grief.
rows.anchor: they can eat and drink to their heart’s content.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haniʾ means something very suitable or agreeable.
rows.anchor: It means something which is very suitable.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haniʾ is an adjective qualifying an omitted verbal noun, with the implied construction “eating pleasantly.”
rows.anchor: Here, as an adjective, it qualifies a suppressed verbal noun.

rows.speaker: some people
rows.claim: Some grammarians parse haniʾ as an accusative of state.
rows.anchor: Some people regard it to be an accusative of state

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi rejects the accusative-of-state analysis as contrary to grammatical principles.
rows.anchor: However, this view is against grammatical principles.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muttakiʾin explains fakihin in verse 18; verse 19 is parenthetical, and the believers enjoy their Lord's gifts while reclining on thrones in rows.
rows.anchor: Verse nineteen is a parenthetical sentence.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rows of thrones depict beautifully ordered seats and imply that the believers are intimate and frank with one another, facing each other.
rows.anchor: sitting on thrones arranged in consecutive rows.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will complete believers' enjoyment by granting them their spouses and children; the wording gives only a broad indication, while the true form is known to God and will be clear in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: A person’s enjoyment is incomplete without his wife and children.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers' children who followed their parents in faith will be reunited with them in Paradise even if their own deeds and faith would not earn the same rank.
rows.anchor: those among their children who followed their parents in faith will be united with them there

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Children at a lower level of faith are raised to their parents' rank by grace, while the parents' own reward and rank are not diminished.
rows.anchor: Children having a lower level of faith will be upgraded to the status of the parents without reducing the latter’s status.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mention of faith restricts this concession to children who themselves profess faith; faithless children do not qualify even if they claim to have followed their parents.
rows.anchor: this concession is reserved only for those children who followed their parents in professing faith.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because “faith” is indefinite here, Islahi infers that faith has levels and even the lowest level in Paradise qualifies for the concession.
rows.anchor: it is evident that it has levels.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Salvation is based on each person's faith and deeds, which alone save or ruin; ancestry or outward association with virtue cannot save the faithless or those without good deeds.
rows.anchor: express God’s principle of salvation: each person will be judged on his deeds.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This is also a warning to Jews and Arabian idolaters who corrupted Abraham's and Ishmael's religion yet expected high Paradise rank merely through descent.
rows.anchor: a warning to both the Jews and the Idolaters of Arabia.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: There is no contradiction between deed-based salvation and raising faithful children: the latter is an additional grace God reserves for the faithful.
rows.anchor: this matter relates to God’s graciousness which He has reserved for the faithful.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse also permits the reverse inference: faithful parents may be raised to a higher rank occupied by their children to complete their joy, despite not earning that rank by their own deeds.
rows.anchor: The reverse can also be deduced from this verse:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reverse elevation is supported by the equal affection between parents and children, whether the parents are being joined to children or children to parents.
rows.anchor: affection found between parents and children is the same found between children and parents.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For true believers, the greatest concern for their children is their safety in the Hereafter and from Hell; worldly success is secondary.
rows.anchor: the greatest worry which occupies his mind regarding his children is that the Almighty save them from the horrors of the Hereafter

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets' and righteous people's prayers for their children prioritize success in the Hereafter as the real concern.
rows.anchor: in the prayers made by the Prophets and the righteous for their children, success in the Hereafter is mentioned in preference

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The early believers shared this concern for their children's afterlife, as reflected in their statement in 52:26 that they had previously feared for their families.
rows.anchor: This concern is evident from verse 26 of this very sūrah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Islahi explains the fear for one's family as concern for a flock entrusted by God, so that an animal not be lost to a wolf; analogously, believers hoped their children would receive faith and avoid Hell, just as God led them out of ignorance.
rows.anchor: the fact that a goat of the herd they were made a shepherd of by the Almighty should not be devoured by a wolf

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These glad tidings assure believers that God may reunite even lower-ranking believing children with them without reducing the parents' rank, raising the children instead.
rows.anchor: the Almighty will be further gracious to them: If their children followed them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People should guide close relatives toward faith: without faith no one succeeds in the Hereafter, even a prophet's descendant, while believing offspring, however low their faith, may join their parents.
rows.anchor: each person should try to guide his close ones to the path of faith as much as possible.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As well as reuniting their families, God will provide the believers with more of the fruits and meat they desire.
rows.anchor: He will provide even more of their cherished fruits and meat to them.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word amd points to provision increasing along with the increase in the number of people reunited.
rows.anchor: with the increase in number, their provisions and sustenance will also increase.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The paired terms for fruit and meat encompass all favors involving food.
rows.anchor: combine in them all the favours related to edibles
